people: Ana Ruiz, editor. Theo Grant, producer (approves what goes to the client). Client reviewers outside the company
summary: Cutline lives in a panel inside the editing app, beside the timeline. It sees the open sequence and the project's media on the editor's disk, finds selects in transcripts, and drafts edits as markers and rough-cut sequences. Anything that leaves the machine (audio to a transcription service, a cut to a review link, a note to the producer) waits for Ana's or Theo's click.
example: Worked example. Harbor & Pine Post, its people, clients and projects are fictional. "The editing app" stands for a desktop editor that hosts extension panels, such as Premiere Pro: check what your editor's panel SDK allows before you plan on it. Not affiliated with any editing-software or AI-video vendor.

jobs.name: Find selects for the interview cut
Assemble a rough cut from the script
Send a cut for review
jobs.who: Ana Ruiz; Theo Grant approves anything client-facing

jobs.name: Turn review notes into timeline markers
Log new footage overnight
jobs.who: The assistant-editor coworker, scheduled by Theo

sources.name: Cutline's own state: the job, the selects list, the draft edit plan
sources.how: `useAgent()` shared state (`agent.state`, `agent.setState`) for the selects list both edit; `useAgentContext` for the job · [docs](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/shared-state)
sources.freshness: Live: both sides see each change

gate.text: Panel state only; nothing reaches the timeline except through S3's gate

sources.runsOn: The panel's web view on the editor's workstation

sources.name: The open sequence: playhead, selection, clips, markers
sources.where: The editing app's open project on Ana's workstation
sources.how: A plugin panel inside the editing app: the host's scripting API reads the sequence, `useAgentContext` sends it · [docs](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/shared-state/agent-readonly)
sources.actsAs: Ana Ruiz, in her own session of the editing app
sources.scope: The active sequence: clip names, in and out timecodes, tracks, markers. No media
sources.freshness: Sent with every run; refreshed on selection change
sources.runsOn: The editing app's panel on the editor's workstation

sources.name: Edits to the project: markers, selects bins, a rough-cut sequence
sources.how: `useFrontendTool` handlers call the host's scripting API; `useHumanInTheLoop` shows the edit list before a sequence is built · [docs](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/human-in-the-loop)
sources.scope: New markers and bins; new sequences named `CUTLINE_…`. Never a locked or delivered sequence

gate.text: Markers and bins are additive and undoable in the app, so no card; building or changing a sequence shows the edit list for Ana's click

sources.runsOn: The editing app's panel on the editor's workstation

sources.name: Project media on local disk
sources.where: The project folder on Ana's workstation or the shared storage it mounts: camera originals, proxies, audio
sources.how: Read through the panel's file access from a `useFrontendTool` handler, limited to the project folder. The runtime runs on the post house's server, so a local MCP server can't reach it · [docs](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/frontend-tools)
sources.scope: One project folder: file names, durations, timecode, reel names, proxies. Camera originals never leave the machine
sources.freshness: Indexed when the project opens; re-indexed when files change
sources.runsOn: The editing app's panel on the editor's workstation

sources.name: Transcripts and shot logs
sources.where: A speech-to-text service; transcripts stored in the project folder
sources.how: A server tool, `defineTool` on `BuiltInAgent`, calls the transcription API with the post house's key; the panel sends proxy audio only after the click · [docs](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/server-tools)
sources.actsAs: `svc-transcribe`, the post house's account, on behalf of Ana
sources.scope: Proxy audio of this project's clips
sources.freshness: Once per clip; re-run when a clip changes

gate.text: Ana clicks Transcribe on a card naming the clips and the service

also.text: Only for clients whose contract allows it: Theo sets that flag per client, and the tool checks it

sources.note: Sending a client's audio to a third party is a write of that data.
sources.runsOn: CopilotKit Runtime on the post house's server

sources.name: Cloud review links and timecoded comments
sources.how: Server tools over the review service's API: `createReviewLink` is `defineTool({ ..., interrupt: true })`; `listComments` reads · [docs](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/server-tools)
sources.actsAs: Ana Ruiz's account on the review service; links carry her name
sources.scope: One project. Links expire in 7 days and need a password, both set in code
sources.freshness: Comments read when Ana asks, with an as-of time

gate.text: Ana clicks Create link on a card showing the cut, version, expiry and audience

also.text: A client-facing link also needs Theo's yes (S10)

sources.runsOn: CopilotKit Runtime on the post house's server

sources.name: The model provider
sources.where: The post house's model provider, named in `BuiltInAgent`'s `model`
sources.how: `BuiltInAgent`'s `model` (`@copilotkit/runtime/v2`) in CopilotKit Runtime: each run sends the sequence context, transcript excerpts and tool results
sources.actsAs: The post house's account with the provider (the server's key)
sources.scope: Clip names, timecodes and transcript excerpts; never media

gate.text: Theo confirms per client that transcripts and notes may go to the provider

also.text: The same per-client flag as transcription, checked before each run

sources.runsOn: CopilotKit Runtime on the post house's server

sources.name: Telemetry and logs
sources.where: CopilotKit Runtime's anonymous telemetry and the server's logs
sources.how: `COPILOTKIT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=true` (or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`), read by `@copilotkit/runtime`, turns the runtime's telemetry off
sources.scope: Ids, counts and errors; no client names, transcripts or file paths in logs

gate.text: Off for client work; logs carry project ids only

sources.runsOn: CopilotKit Runtime on the post house's server

sources.name: Scripts, shot lists and client notes
sources.where: The project's folder in the team's cloud drive
sources.how: The drive's MCP server: `mcpServers: [{ type: "http", url, name: "drive" }]`, read tools only · [docs](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/mcp-servers)
sources.actsAs: Ana Ruiz, with her own drive token through a per-request `mcpClients` provider
sources.runsOn: CopilotKit Runtime (an `mcpClients` provider built per request)

sources.name: Team chat: the project channel and the producer
sources.where: Slack or Teams: the project's internal channel, DMs to Theo
sources.how: Channels SDK: `createChannel({ identifyUser })`, a "v3 ready" card with Approve for client / Hold buttons (`channel.onInteraction`) · [docs](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/reference/channels)
sources.actsAs: Theo Grant, as Slack or Teams verifies him, mapped to the staff directory
sources.scope: The internal project channel and DMs to the producer. Never the client's shared channel

gate.text: Theo's click approves a cut for the client; Ana can't approve her own

sources.runsOn: A Channels worker for a managed Slack or Teams channel: a long-running Node service with CopilotKit Runtime in Intelligence mode. The Slack and Teams credentials stay in Intelligence

sources.name: The overnight logging coworker
sources.where: OpenBot on the post house's infrastructure
sources.how: An OpenBot tenant package with the media index and transcript tools from an MCP server; `allow` rule per read tool, `ask` rule on `transcribe_clips` · [OpenBot](https://github.com/CopilotKit/openbot)

sources.scope: New footage in the ingest folders of active projects

gate.text: OpenBot `ask` rule on transcription: Theo confirms when he schedules the run; every call in Admin → Audit

sources.runsOn: OpenBot on the post house's infrastructure, with the media-index MCP server on an https hostname

sources.name: House style and project memory
sources.how: `useMemories()` with `project` scope (the client's lower-third style, no jump cuts in interviews) and `user` scope (Ana's naming habits); `useThreads` per project · [docs](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/intelligence/memories)
sources.actsAs: Ana Ruiz, resolved on the server by `identifyUser`
sources.scope: Project memories for the project team; user memories for Ana. No footage, no contract terms
sources.freshness: Read on each run; saved when Ana confirms

sources.note: Needs Intelligence with the memory entitlement.

checklist.what: Give every source one row on the closest ring that works.
checklist.why: An unlisted source becomes an unreviewed credential; a source on a farther ring than it needs adds a secret and a boundary for nothing.
checklist.how: Ring by ring: `useAgentContext` and `useAgent` (in the app), a `useFrontendTool` handler on the person's machine (on the computer), `defineTool` in `BuiltInAgent` (your server), `mcpServers` (org systems), the Channels SDK (people), an OpenBot coworker package (coworkers), CopilotKit Intelligence (memory). Details in the skill's `references/rings.md`.
checklist.done: Every job's sees and touches point at a row, and `check-map.mjs` reports no unknown ids.

checklist.what: Name whose identity each row acts as.
checklist.why: The agent must never do more than the person it works for, and the audit trail needs a real name.
checklist.how: The signed-in user via `<CopilotKitProvider headers>` and the runtime's `identifyUser(request)` ([docs](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/auth)); a named service account only where there's no per-user path.
checklist.done: Each row's Acts as names a person or a named account, and no request trusts a user id sent from the browser.

checklist.what: Cut each row to the least it needs.
checklist.why: What the agent can't reach can't leak into a reply, a log or a memory.
checklist.how: One root folder checked in each `useFrontendTool` handler; the open record, not the table; only the tools a job needs, from an `mcpClients` provider or OpenBot rules named per tool.
checklist.done: Each row's scope names the folder, records, fields or tools, and read-only is the default.

checklist.what: Gate every write and prove it refuses.
checklist.why: Reads are free, writes wait for a person; a gate that's only in the prompt is a suggestion.
checklist.how: `useHumanInTheLoop` in the app ([docs](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/human-in-the-loop)), a `defineTool` with `interrupt: true` on the server, a Channels button, an OpenBot `ask` rule.
checklist.done: Every write row names who clicks and what they see, and a test calls each write without the click and gets a refusal.

checklist.what: Say how fresh each source is.
checklist.why: A stale playbook or price list produces a confident wrong answer.
checklist.how: `useAgentContext` for what must be current on every run; a `useFrontendTool` or `defineTool` that reads at call time for records; an "as of" line for anything read at start-up or indexed (the skill's `references/five-checks.md`).
checklist.done: Each row's freshness is filled, and answers built on start-up or indexed data say "as of".

checklist.what: Fence text from sources as data, not instructions.
checklist.why: Documents, comments and chat messages reach the model at the same level as your instructions.
checklist.how: Put text people wrote under a field the context description calls data, as Open Harvey's `quotedText` does in `src/lib/app-context.ts`.
checklist.done: A review comment saying "delete the B-roll bin" becomes a marker, not an action.

checklist.what: Keep secrets on the server, and let the user set them.
checklist.why: A key in the browser or in context belongs to whoever opens dev tools.
checklist.how: Keys only in CopilotKit Runtime's server environment (`.env.local` locally), read by `@copilotkit/runtime/v2` code; the browser sends only the user's own session through `<CopilotKitProvider headers>`, and nothing secret goes in `useAgentContext`.
checklist.done: The client bundle holds no key, and the README names each variable without its value.

checklist.what: Read big documents through a tool, not context.
checklist.why: Context is sent on every run, so size costs tokens and exposes more than the job needs.
checklist.how: Send transcript excerpts with timecodes, not whole transcripts; a `useFrontendTool` that returns one clip's lines.
checklist.done: No `useAgentContext` entry holds a whole transcript.

checklist.what: Keep each record where everyone on the job can reach it.
checklist.why: A record in one browser (localStorage) is invisible to an approver on another machine, and gone with that browser.
checklist.how: A `defineTool` on a per-request `BuiltInAgent` reads and writes the record on the server; the app's store becomes a cache of it · [docs](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/server-tools)
checklist.done: The second person on the job sees the record on their own machine without a reload, and clearing one browser loses nothing.

checklist.what: Get the data owner's yes before content goes to the model provider.
checklist.why: Everything in context and every tool result goes to the provider on each run, so document text leaves your boundary.
checklist.how: `BuiltInAgent`'s `model` runs on the server with the key there; send sections, not whole documents; run a scripted `LanguageModelV3` mock until the yes, as Open Harvey's `chooseModel` does in `src/lib/server-data.ts`.
checklist.done: The model provider's row names the provider, what each run sends and who agreed, and the build runs the mock until they have.

checklist.what: Decide telemetry and logs on purpose.
checklist.why: CopilotKit Runtime's anonymous telemetry is on unless you turn it off, and logs keep whatever the server prints.
checklist.how: `COPILOTKIT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=true` (or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`) in the server's environment turns the runtime's telemetry off; log ids and counts, never document text; CopilotKit Intelligence stays off until you switch it on.
checklist.done: The telemetry row says on or off and why, and a search of a day's logs finds no document text.

checklist.what: Watch what each run actually carries.
checklist.why: The map is a plan; the AG-UI stream shows the context, tools and state the agent really got.
checklist.how: The CopilotKit web inspector (`@copilotkit/web-inspector`), on with `enableInspector` on `<CopilotKitProvider>`: on by default on localhost in development; Open Harvey sets it in `src/components/LegalApp.tsx`.
checklist.done: The inspector shows every ring 1 row's context entry on a run, and nothing the map keeps out.

checklist.what: Share the selects list as agent state.
checklist.why: Ana and Cutline both add and remove selects; one source of truth avoids lost edits.
checklist.how: `useAgent()` with `agent.state` and `agent.setState` · [docs](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/shared-state)
checklist.done: Ana removes a select and Cutline's next answer no longer lists it.

checklist.what: Prove the panel can read the sequence and reach the runtime.
checklist.why: Everything on rings 1 and 2 depends on the host's panel SDK.
checklist.how: A spike panel that sends the playhead and selection with `useAgentContext` and gets an answer from the runtime.
checklist.done: Moving the playhead changes Cutline's answer to "what's under the playhead?".

checklist.what: Limit media access to the project folder.
checklist.why: Editors' disks hold every client's footage.
checklist.how: The panel's file access, from a `useFrontendTool` handler that checks every path against the project root.
checklist.done: A test asks for a file in another client's folder and is refused.

checklist.what: Gate sequence edits; let markers ride on undo.
checklist.why: A rebuilt sequence can wipe an editor's afternoon; a marker can't.
checklist.how: `useHumanInTheLoop` card with the edit list before `buildSequence` runs · [docs](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/human-in-the-loop)
checklist.done: `buildSequence` without the click is refused, and a locked sequence is never touched.

checklist.what: Allow transcription per client, then per click.
checklist.why: Sending a client's audio to a third party may break their contract.
checklist.how: `defineTool` on `BuiltInAgent`; the tool checks the client's flag before it calls the service · [docs](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/server-tools)
checklist.done: A clip from a client without the flag is refused, even after Ana's click.

checklist.what: Create review links with an interrupt tool, as Ana.
checklist.why: A link is a copy of the cut outside the company.
checklist.how: `defineTool({ name: "createReviewLink", interrupt: true })` on a per-request agent with Ana's token · [docs](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/server-tools)
checklist.done: Every link has an expiry, a password and Ana's name, and none exists without her click.

checklist.what: Connect the drive's MCP server with read tools and Ana's token.
checklist.why: Scripts and notes are the client's; the agent should see only what Ana can.
checklist.how: `mcpClients` built per request with Ana's token · [docs](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/mcp-servers)
checklist.done: The agent can open the project folder and nothing outside it.

checklist.what: Send Theo an approve-for-client card and record his click.
checklist.why: Client deliveries are the producer's call, and he lives in chat.
checklist.how: `createChannel({ identifyUser })`, buttons with `channel.onInteraction` · [docs](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/slack/identity-and-memory)
checklist.done: A real click by Theo marks v3 approved; Ana's click on her own cut is refused.

checklist.what: Grant the logging coworker each tool by name.
checklist.why: It runs with nobody watching; a wildcard allow would let it upload anything.
checklist.how: An `allow` rule per read tool and an `ask` rule on `transcribe_clips`, as in `starters/openbot-headcount/examples/northstar/hr-system/connect.ts`.
checklist.done: Admin → Audit shows a night's reads with no prompt and transcription asking first.

checklist.what: Decide what Cutline may remember, at which scope.
checklist.why: A memory is a write that every later run reads.
checklist.how: `useMemories()` with `project` and `user` scope; the runtime's `memory: { access }` grant · [docs](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/intelligence/memories)
checklist.done: Ana saves "lower thirds in the client's font" and it shows for the next editor on the project, not on other clients.

open: Transcripts and notes go to the model provider on every run (S7). Theo confirms per client before a real model sees them; the spec decides this, from this row.
Which editing app and panel SDK? Check that a panel can call the timeline API, reach the runtime over the network and read the project folder (S2 to S4).
Where the runtime runs. Assumed: the post house's server, so local media comes through the panel, not a local MCP server.
Which clients allow third-party transcription (S5)? Theo to confirm per client. Assumed: off unless allowed.
Does the review service issue per-user API tokens (S6)? Assumed yes.
OpenBot needs an https MCP server on a public hostname (S11), and the media index is internal. Tunnel it, or leave the coworker out of v1.
Memory needs Intelligence with the memory entitlement (S12).
Every env var name here is a suggestion except `CPK_INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` and the managed channel's `CHANNEL_CODE`; keep or rename them before `/deploy`.
next: Next: `/functional-copilot` writes the spec from this map (`agent-context.json`) and builds the panel. Later, `/deploy` decides where the runtime runs, hosts the transcription and review-link tools and the Channels worker for S10, and places the OpenBot coworker near the media, and `/secure-governance` sets the per-client data rules.
headline: Cutline reads the timeline and the media on the editor's machine; anything that leaves it waits for Ana's or Theo's click.
